mainTopic: How hot and cold foods transfer taste (רב: עילאה גבר vs. שמואל: תתאה גבר), tested against the משנה about the gravy of the קרבן פסח dripping onto earthenware and flour.
overview: This amud asks how taste passes between foods when one falls onto another. Hot into hot is forbidden and cold into cold is permitted, according to everyone. רב and שמואל argue about mixed cases: רב says the top item decides (עילאה גבר), and שמואל says the bottom item decides (תתאה גבר). The גמרא tests both views against the משנה about the קרבן פסח: gravy dripping onto earthenware, gravy dripping onto flour, and the פסח smeared with oil of תרומה. Each case fits רב, and שמואל's side answers each challenge: the earthenware and flour were hot, and smearing uses only a tiny amount of oil. Two ברייתות then support שמואל, after the גמרא corrects their wording so that hot falling into cold needs peeling and cold into cold needs only rinsing. רב הונא adds that salted food is forbidden even when cold, because שמואל said salted food is like boiling food and pickled food is like cooked food. רבא limits that rule to food too salty to eat, which explains why רב חיננא permitted a bird that fell into כמכא, with limits for a roasted, cracked, or spiced bird. The amud ends as a new statement of רב begins.

steps.title: The cases everyone agrees on
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the agreed cases: hot into hot is forbidden, and cold into cold is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Hot into hot, everyone agrees, is] forbidden. Cold into cold, everyone agrees, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out the simple cases where a forbidden food falls onto a permitted food. Then it moves to the disputed cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אָסוּר ends the previous sentence: if a hot forbidden food falls into a hot permitted food, everything becomes forbidden, because heat makes the taste soak in. If both are cold, no taste is absorbed, so the food is permitted. Usually it only needs to be rinsed. These two clear cases are the background for the argument that follows.
steps.confusionAlert: The first word אָסוּר is not a new statement. It is the end of the sentence 'hot into hot, everyone agrees it is forbidden,' which began on the previous daf.

phrases.english: [Hot into hot, all agree it] is forbidden.
phrases.notes: End of a sentence from the previous daf.

phrases.english: Cold into cold —
all agree it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: צוֹנֵן לְתוֹךְ צוֹנֵן דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of cases from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hot into hot is forbidden, and cold into cold is permitted, according to everyone.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about mixed temperatures
steps.stepSummary: רב says the upper item decides. שמואל says the lower item decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hot into cold, or cold into hot: רב said the upper one wins. שמואל said the lower one wins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents the argument between רב and שמואל about what happens when one food is hot and the other is cold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the top food sets the temperature: hot on top heats the bottom food, and cold on top cools it. For שמואל, the bottom food sets the temperature: a hot bottom heats what lands on it, and a cold bottom cools it. Everything that follows tests these two views.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: the top decides (עילאה גבר). שמואל: the bottom decides (תתאה גבר).
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument is the source for many practical laws of mixing foods (בשר בחלב and similar cases), and later פוסקים build on it.

phrases.english: Hot into cold,
and cold into hot,
Rav said: the upper one prevails.
And Shmuel said: the lower one prevails.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר עִילָּאָה גָּבַר וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר תַּתָּאָה גָּבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the agreed cases to the disputed ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In mixed-temperature cases, רב says the upper item sets the outcome and שמואל says the lower item does.

steps.title: The earthenware case fits רב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about gravy dripping on cold earthenware makes sense according to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if gravy dripped onto earthenware and went back onto the פסח, remove that spot. Assume the earthenware is cold. For רב this works: the hot gravy heats the earthenware, the earthenware heats the gravy back, and when the gravy returns to the פסח, the meat is roasted by the earthenware's heat. The Torah says 'roasted by fire,' not roasted by something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה about the קרבן פסח and shows that it fits רב. This is setting up a challenge to שמואל, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes the earthenware was cold. According to רב, the hot gravy on top heats the earthenware, and the hot earthenware then cooks the gravy. When that gravy drips back, the part of the פסח it touches is cooked by earthenware heat, not by fire. That breaks the rule of צלי אש, so that spot must be cut away.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind (an initial assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the meat touched something forbidden. The problem is that part of the פסח would be cooked by something other than direct fire, and the קרבן פסח must be roasted by fire alone.

phrases.english: We learned: if some of its gravy dripped onto the earthenware
and returned to it — he must remove its place.
It enters your mind that this refers to cold earthenware.
Granted, according to Rav who said 'the upper one prevails,'
for this reason he must remove its place —
for the gravy goes and heats the earthenware,
and then the earthenware heats the gravy.
And when the gravy returns onto the Paschal lamb —

phrases.aramaic: קָא מִטְּוֵי פֶּסַח מֵחֲמַת חַמִּימוּתָא דְחֶרֶס,
phrases.english: the Paschal lamb is roasted by the heat of the earthenware,
and the Merciful One said 'roasted by fire,'
and not roasted by means of something else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the argument in step 2 against a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the upper item prevails
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: נטף מרוטבו על החרס... יטול את מקומו

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל from the earthenware case
steps.stepSummary: According to שמואל, cold earthenware would cool the gravy, so why cut away the spot?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to שמואל, who says the lower one wins, the earthenware is cold and would cool the gravy. So why must he remove the spot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the same משנה seems not to fit his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the cold earthenware on the bottom wins and cools the gravy. Cooled gravy cannot cook the פסח, so nothing should need to be cut away. Yet the משנה says to remove the spot.

phrases.english: But according to Shmuel who said 'the lower one prevails,'
the earthenware, since it is cold —
cools down the gravy,
why must he remove its place?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second half of the בשלמא structure: it fits רב, but not שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that the lower item prevails
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cold earthenware on the bottom should cool the gravy under שמואל's rule, so the משנה's requirement to remove the spot makes no sense.

steps.title: The earthenware was hot
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי ירמיה's report in שמואל's name about hot flour, the earthenware here was also hot.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי ירמיה said in the name of שמואל: the flour case is about hot flour. Here too, it is about hot earthenware.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל by saying the משנה is talking about earthenware that was already hot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the earthenware was cold, but that was only an assumption (קא סלקא דעתך). רבי ירמיה reported that שמואל explained the flour case as hot flour, and the same applies here. Hot earthenware is a case of hot meeting hot, which is a problem according to everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's side reads the משנה as hot earthenware, so it no longer proves anything for רב.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yirmeya said in the name of Shmuel:
[the case is] with hot flour,
here too, with hot earthenware.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (the earthenware was hot, not cold)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earthenware was cold, so שמואל would say the gravy cools down.
steps.terutzMaskana: The earthenware was hot, so the gravy stays hot and roasts the פסח even according to שמואל.

steps.title: The flour case also fits רב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about gravy dripping on flour, if the flour is cold, fits רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if gravy dripped onto flour, take a handful from that spot. Assume the flour is cold. For רב this works: the gravy heats the flour around it, the flour heats the gravy back, and the gravy is roasted by the flour's heat. The Torah says 'roasted by fire,' not by something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, gravy on flour, and shows that it fits רב. This sets up a challenge to שמואל that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure is the same as the earthenware case. The flour is assumed cold, and according to רב the hot gravy on top heats the flour. The heated flour then cooks the gravy, which is not 'roasted by fire,' so that handful of flour must be removed.

keyTerms.meaning: He takes a handful (removes a fistful)

phrases.english: We learned: if some of its gravy dripped onto the flour
he must take a handful from its place.
It enters your mind that this refers to cold flour.
Granted, according to Rav who said 'the upper one prevails,'
for this reason he must take a handful from its place —
for it heats the flour that is around it,
and then the flour heats it [the gravy],

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מִטְּוֵי רוֹטֶב מֵחֲמַת חַמִּימוּתָא דְסוֹלֶת,
phrases.english: and the gravy is roasted by the heat of the flour,
and the Merciful One said 'roasted by fire,'
and not roasted by means of something else.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן נָטַף מֵרוֹטְבּוֹ עַל הַסּוֹלֶת יִקְמוֹץ אֶת מְקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a parallel test using the next case in the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the upper item prevails
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: נטף מרוטבו על הסולת יקמוץ את מקומו

steps.title: Why remove a whole handful of cold flour according to שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: According to שמואל, cold flour on the bottom should cool the gravy. So why does the משנה require removing a whole handful instead of just a small spot?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to שמואל, who says the lower item decides: flour that is cold cools the gravy down. So why does the משנה say to remove a handful from that place? Removing just the spot itself should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל from the flour case in the משנה. If the cold flour underneath cools the gravy, very little should need to be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל's rule, cold flour on the bottom wins and cools the hot gravy. Then the flour never heats up and never roasts the gravy, so removing only the spot where the gravy landed should be enough. The משנה's demand for a full handful implies that the heated flour roasted the gravy around it, which fits רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove a handful (a קמיצה) from its place
Remove just its place (only the spot)

phrases.english: But according to Shmuel, who said 'the lower one prevails,'
the flour, since it is cold,
cools it (the gravy) down;
why do I need 'he must remove a handful from its place'?
(It should be enough for him to remove just its place!)
phrases.notes: This whole line is in round brackets, so some versions leave it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 6 showed the flour case fits רב. Now the same case is used to attack שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that the lower item decides
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cold flour underneath should cool the gravy, so only light absorption happens. That means only the spot should need removal, not a full handful.

steps.title: The flour was hot
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה, in שמואל's name, says the משנה is talking about hot flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of שמואל: the משנה is talking about hot flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the flour in the משנה was hot. Then even according to שמואל, the bottom item is hot and the absorption goes deep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the flour underneath is hot, שמואל's rule gives the same result as רב's. The hot flour roasts the gravy around it, which is not צלי אש, so a whole handful must be removed. This is the same answer already used for the earthenware in Step 5.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Shmuel said:
It is referring to hot flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the flour was hot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The flour was assumed to be cold, so under שמואל it would cool the gravy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The flour was hot, so the lower item heats the gravy and roasts it, which is not צלי אש. A full handful must be removed even according to שמואל.

steps.title: Smearing the קרבן פסח with oil of תרומה fits רב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a roasted קרבן פסח of ישראלים smeared with oil of תרומה only needs its outer layer peeled. This fits רב, because the oil on top is cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if one smeared the קרבן פסח with oil of תרומה, and it belongs to a group of כהנים, they may eat it. If it belongs to ישראלים: if it is raw, he rinses it; if it is roasted, he peels off the outer layer. This works well for רב, who says the upper item decides. That is why peeling is enough, since the upper item (the oil) is cold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה about oil of תרומה smeared on the קרבן פסח. It shows this case fits רב's view nicely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cold oil is on top and the hot roasted meat is underneath. According to רב, the cold upper item wins, so the oil only soaks into the surface. That is why peeling off the outer layer is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion given to the כהן; forbidden to a ישראל
A group of כהנים eating the פסח together
He must peel off the outer layer

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna:
If one smeared it with teruma oil,
if it is a group of priests, they may eat it.
If it belongs to Israelites,
if it is raw, he must rinse it;

phrases.aramaic: אִם צָלִי הוּא — יִקְלוֹף אֶת הַחִיצוֹן.
phrases.english: if it is roasted, he must peel off the outer layer.
Granted, according to Rav, who said 'the upper one prevails,'
for this reason peeling is enough for it,
because the upper one (the oil) is cold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the flour case is settled, the גמרא opens a new test case from a different משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that the upper item decides
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about smearing the roasted פסח with oil of תרומה, where only peeling is required

steps.title: According to שמואל, the hot meat should absorb the oil completely
steps.stepSummary: According to שמואל, the hot meat underneath wins and absorbs the oil. So why is peeling enough? The whole פסח should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to שמואל, who says the lower item decides: since the meat is hot, it absorbs the oil. Why is peeling enough? It should be forbidden completely!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל from the oil case. If the hot meat on the bottom wins, the oil should soak all the way in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל, the hot lower item heats the oil, and it is absorbed deeply into the meat. That would make the whole קרבן forbidden to ישראלים. So the משנה's ruling that peeling is enough looks like a problem for שמואל.

phrases.english: But according to Shmuel, who said 'the lower one prevails,'
since it (the meat) is hot, it absorbs;
why is peeling enough for it?
It should be entirely forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמַר תַּתָּאָה גָּבַר כֵּיוָן דְּחַם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 9 showed the oil case fits רב. Now it is turned against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that the lower item decides
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The hot meat underneath should make the oil soak in deeply, which should forbid the whole פסח, not just its surface.

steps.title: Smearing uses only a tiny amount
steps.stepSummary: Smearing is different, because only a tiny amount of oil is used. So even if it is absorbed, it does not forbid the whole פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Smearing is different, because it is done with only a tiny amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. The oil case is special because smearing uses very little oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer agrees that, under שמואל, the hot meat absorbs. But such a small amount of oil cannot spread through and forbid the entire קרבן, so peeling the outside is enough. The issue here is the amount of the forbidden substance, not which item is hotter.

phrases.english: Smearing is different,
because it is done with only a minute amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hot meat absorbing the oil should forbid the whole פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because smearing uses only a tiny bit of oil, it is not enough to forbid the whole פסח. Peeling is enough even according to שמואל.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the meat stops absorbing under שמואל. It says the amount of oil is too small to forbid everything.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that whenever the lower item is hot, the food is forbidden, and whenever the lower item is cold, rinsing is enough. This matches שמואל exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that matches שמואל: hot into hot is forbidden. And likewise, cold put into hot is forbidden. Hot into cold, and cold into cold, one rinses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports שמואל. Its rulings depend completely on whether the bottom item is hot or cold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key cases are the mixed ones. Cold falling into hot is forbidden, because the hot bottom wins. Hot falling into cold only needs rinsing, because the cold bottom wins. Both rulings follow שמואל and go against רב, who would say the item on top decides.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with him
He rinses it (and it stays permitted)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports שמואל: what matters is the item on the bottom. Hot on the bottom means forbidden; cold on the bottom means rinsing is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the clearest support for שמואל's rule, and it becomes the basis for the practical הלכה of תתאה גבר.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Shmuel:
Hot into hot is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן צוֹנֵן שֶׁנָּתַן לְתוֹךְ חַם — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: And so too, cold that one put into hot is forbidden.
Hot into cold
and cold into cold: one rinses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending שמואל against two challenges, the גמרא brings positive support for him.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that the lower item decides
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: cold into hot is forbidden, while hot into cold only needs rinsing

steps.title: How can hot food falling into cold food need only rinsing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's line that hot food falling into cold food only needs rinsing. The hot food must absorb a little before it cools.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hot into cold, you just rinse? Since the top item is hot, it cannot avoid soaking in a little before the cold item cools it down. It should at least need peeling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks one line of the ברייתא from step 12: 'hot falling into cold, just rinse.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the cold bottom item wins in the end, cooling takes a moment. During that moment the hot top item absorbs a little of the forbidden taste. A little absorption means at least the outer layer should be peeled off (קליפה). Rinsing alone (הדחה) should not be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He rinses (washing off the surface is enough)

steps.confusionAlert: There are three levels here. Rinsing (הדחה) means nothing was absorbed. Peeling (קליפה) means only the outer layer absorbed. Fully forbidden (אסור) means the taste went all the way through. Keep these three apart.

phrases.english: Hot into cold — one rinses?!
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא's line in surprise

phrases.english: Since it is hot,
until [the cold item] cools it down —
it is impossible that it does not absorb a little,
it should at least require peeling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one clause inside the ברייתא that was just brought as support for שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's clause 'חם לתוך צונן מדיח'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hot item must absorb a little before it cools. So rinsing alone cannot be enough. At least peeling is needed.

steps.title: Corrected reading: hot into cold needs peeling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording. Hot into cold needs peeling. Cold into cold needs only rinsing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: hot into cold, you peel. Cold into cold, you rinse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text now has three clear levels. The bottom item hot means fully forbidden. Hot on top of cold means peeling. Cold on cold means rinsing. This still fits שמואל's idea that the bottom item wins (תתאה גבר). The hot top item absorbs only a thin layer before the cold bottom item cools it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (the text should read this way)
He peels off the outer layer

steps.whatToRemember: Bottom item hot means forbidden. Hot on cold means peel. Cold on cold means rinse.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
hot into cold — one peels,
cold into cold — one rinses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say hot falling into cold needs only rinsing
steps.terutzMaskana: Hot falling into cold needs peeling. Only cold falling into cold is fixed by rinsing.

steps.title: A second ברייתא about meat and milk
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא rules that hot meat in hot milk, or cold meat in hot milk, is forbidden. Hot or cold meat in cold milk only needs rinsing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: boiling meat that fell into boiling milk, and cold meat that fell into hot milk, is forbidden. Hot meat into cold milk, or cold meat into cold milk, you just rinse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same pattern, this time about meat and milk (בשר בחלב).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, everything depends on the bottom item. When the milk below is hot, the meat is forbidden even if the meat itself was cold. This fits שמואל's rule that the bottom item wins. But this ברייתא also says 'hot into cold, rinse,' which sets up the same challenge again.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Another [ברייתא] taught:
Boiling meat that fell
into boiling milk,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן צוֹנֵן שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ חַם — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: and likewise cold [meat] that fell into hot [milk] — it is forbidden.
Hot into cold
and cold into cold — one rinses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא with the same structure as the one in step 12
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that the bottom item decides (תתאה גבר)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא about meat falling into milk

steps.title: The same challenge to the second ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the second ברייתא. Hot meat in cold milk must absorb a little, so it should need peeling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hot into cold, you just rinse? Since it is hot, it must soak in a little before it cools down. It should at least need peeling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the exact challenge from step 13, now aimed at the meat-and-milk ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same as before. The hot meat absorbs some milk in the moment before the cold milk cools it. So rinsing cannot be enough.

phrases.english: Hot into cold — one rinses?!
Since it is hot,
until [the cold item] cools it down —
it is impossible that it does not absorb a little,
it should at least require peeling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the challenge of step 13 to the second ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The second ברייתא's clause 'חם לתוך צונן מדיח'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hot meat must absorb a little milk before it cools. So it needs at least peeling.

steps.title: Same correction for the second ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא is fixed the same way. Hot into cold needs peeling. Cold into cold needs rinsing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: hot into cold, you peel. Cold into cold, you rinse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same fix as in step 14, now for the meat-and-milk ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After this fix, both ברייתות follow the same three-level system. Both fit שמואל's rule that the bottom item wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Into (one item falling on top of the other)
Meat and milk, the topic of this ברייתא

phrases.english: Rather, say:
hot into cold — one peels,
cold into cold — one rinses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 16 the same way step 14 resolved step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hot meat falling into cold milk seemed to need only rinsing
steps.terutzMaskana: Hot meat falling into cold milk needs peeling

steps.title: רב הונא: rinsing is enough only if nothing was salted
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits 'cold into cold, rinse.' It applies only when the food was not salted. If it was salted, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: cold into cold, you rinse. רב הונא said: this was taught only when he did not salt it. But if he salted it, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line 'cold into cold, rinse,' and רב הונא adds a limit to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally two cold foods do not pass taste to each other, so rinsing is enough. רב הונא says salt changes this. If salt is involved, the food is forbidden even though both items are cold.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting the source just learned)
An אמורא, a student of רב
They taught this only in the case of

phrases.english: The Master said:
cold into cold — one rinses.
רב הונא said:
They taught this only where he did not salt it,
but if he salted it — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: צוֹנֵן לְתוֹךְ צוֹנֵן — מֵדִיחַ. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the 'cold into cold' clause of the corrected ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cold falling into cold is fixed by rinsing only if neither item was salted. If one was salted, the food is forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל's source: salted is like boiling, pickled is like cooked
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's reason is שמואל's rule. Salted food counts like boiling food, and pickled food counts like cooked food.
steps.simpleTranslation: As שמואל said: salted food is like boiling food. Pickled food is like cooked food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the basis for רב הונא's ruling, which is a statement of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt draws out and passes taste the way heat does. So a salted cold item acts like a hot one. Pickling, meaning soaking in vinegar or brine, passes taste the way cooking does.

keyTerms.meaning: Pickled (soaked in a liquid such as vinegar or brine)

steps.whyThisMatters: These two rules (מליח כרותח and כבוש כמבושל) are major principles in the laws of mixed foods (תערובות). They are used throughout הלכה, for example when salting meat (מליחה).

phrases.english: As שמואל said:
Salted food is like boiling food.
Pickled food is like cooked food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source and reason for רב הונא's limit
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that salted cold food is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל: מליח הרי הוא כרותח, כבוש הרי הוא כמבושל

steps.title: רבא: the salt rule applies only to food too salty to eat
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits שמואל's rule. Salted food counts like boiling only when it is so salty that it cannot be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: what שמואל said, 'salted food is like boiling food,' applies only when the food cannot be eaten because of its salt. But if it can still be eaten despite its salt, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to שמואל's rule from step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every bit of salt turns food into 'boiling.' Only heavy salting counts, meaning the food is too salty to eat as it is. Lightly salted food that people eat normally does not pass taste like hot food.

keyTerms.meaning: We said (a variant reading; the bracketed version reads שָׁנוּ, 'they taught')

steps.confusionAlert: 'שלא נאכל מחמת מלחו' means the food is TOO salty to eat. That is the case where it counts like boiling food. If it is still eaten despite the salt, the rule does not apply. Do not flip these two cases.
steps.whatToRemember: Salted food counts like boiling food (מליח כרותח), but only when it is too salty to eat.

phrases.english: רבא said:
That which שמואל said,
'salted food is like boiling food' (etc.) —
we said [they taught] it only
phrases.notes: Some versions say אמרן ("we said") and others say שנו ("they taught").

phrases.english: where it is not eaten because of its salt,
but if it is eaten despite its salt — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines and narrows the salted food that שמואל's rule covers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salted food counts like boiling food only when it is too salty to be eaten.

steps.title: A Young Bird Falls Into a Jug of Salty Milk Dip
steps.stepSummary: A young bird fell into a jug of כמכא, a salty dairy dip, and רב חיננא בריה דרבא מפשרוניא ruled it permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain young bird fell into a jug of כמכא, a salty milk dip. רב חיננא, son of רבא of פשרוניא, permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of a real case where meat (a bird) fell into a salty dairy food, and a sage ruled that the bird was permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This looks like it should be forbidden. כמכא is salty, and שמואל said that salted food counts like boiling food (Step 19). Yet רב חיננא permitted it, so the next step will explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: כותח, a salty dip made with milk

phrases.english: A certain young bird
that fell into a jug of kamka (a salty milk dip),
phrases.notes: כמכא is the same as כותח. It contains milk and is quite salty.

phrases.english: Rav Chinana permitted it,
the son of Rava, from Pashronya.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא בַּר גּוֹזָלָא דִּנְפַל לְכַדָּא דְּכַמְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case that shows רבא's limit on שמואל's rule (Step 20) in action.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A young bird that fell into כמכא was ruled permitted.

steps.title: רבא Explains Why the Bird Was Permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא praises רב חיננא and explains his ruling. שמואל's rule covers only food too salty to eat, but כמכא is still eaten despite its salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who is wise enough to permit something like this, if not רב חיננא, son of רבא of פשרוניא? He is a great man. He would tell you: when שמואל said salted food is like boiling food, he meant food that cannot be eaten because of its salt. But this כמכא can still be eaten despite its salt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the lenient ruling by showing that כמכא does not count as 'salted' under שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule makes salted food act like hot, boiling food. רבא's limit (Step 20) says this applies only to food so salty that nobody can eat it. כמכא is salty but still edible, so this is just cold into cold, which only needs rinsing (Step 17).

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, a great scholar
Salted food is like boiling food
It is eaten despite its salt (it is still edible)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'נאכל מחמת מלחו' sounds like 'eaten because of its salt.' Here it means the food is still eaten even though it is salty. In other words, it is not too salty to eat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical example of the rule that salting only turns food into 'boiling' when the food has become too salty to eat.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Who is wise enough to permit
a matter like this,
if not Rav Chinana,
son of Rava from Pashronya,
for he is a great man.
He would say to you:
When Shmuel said
that salted food is like boiling food,
he meant food that cannot be eaten because of its salt;
but this can still be eaten despite its salt.
phrases.notes: So the כמכא is treated as cold, and cold into cold only needs rinsing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאן חַכִּים לְמִישְׁרֵא מִילְּתָא כִּי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the ruling in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: רב חיננא's ruling permitting the bird that fell into כמכא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's limit on שמואל's rule: only food too salty to eat counts as boiling

steps.title: Only a Raw Bird; a Roasted One Needs Peeling
steps.stepSummary: The permission applies only to a raw bird. A roasted bird needs its outer layer peeled off.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to a raw bird. But a roasted bird requires peeling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the lenient ruling: it works only if the bird was raw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roasting softens the meat, so it soaks up flavor more easily. A roasted bird therefore absorbs a little of the milk into its outer layer, and that layer must be peeled off. Rinsing alone is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only (introduces a limit)

phrases.english: And this applies only to a raw bird;
but a roasted one
requires peeling.
phrases.notes: Roasted meat is softer and absorbs more easily.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the lenient ruling of Step 22 to a raw bird.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A raw bird in כמכא only needs rinsing; a roasted bird needs peeling.

steps.title: A Bird With Cracks or Spices Is Forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The bird is permitted only if it has no cracks. If it has cracks, or if it was seasoned with spices, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only when the bird has no cracks. But if it has cracks, it is forbidden. And if it was seasoned with spices, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more limits. Cracks in the bird, or spices on it, make it forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cracks let the milk seep deep inside the meat, so peeling cannot remove it. Spices soften the meat and make it absorb, so it also takes in the milk.

keyTerms.meaning: We said this only (introduces a limit)

steps.whatToRemember: A bird that fell into כמכא needs only rinsing if it is raw, whole, and unspiced. If it is roasted, it needs peeling. If it has cracks or spices, it is forbidden.

phrases.english: And we said this only
when it has no cracks;
but if it has cracks, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The milk gets absorbed into the cracks.

phrases.english: And if it is seasoned with spices, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Spices soften the meat and make it absorb.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ פִּילֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more limits to the lenient ruling, after the raw/roasted limit in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird with cracks, or one seasoned with spices, that fell into כמכא is forbidden.

steps.title: רב Begins a New Statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement from רב, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא is introducing a new statement by רב, and its content comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the attribution אָמַר רַב appears on this amud. The content of רב's statement, and its analysis, come on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav said:
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Transitions from the case of the bird to a new statement by רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only. רב's ruling follows on the next amud.
